header_summary:
The latest developments in the Bitcoin development community include significant enhancements to the Backbone project, which has introduced its 6th public release featuring improved quality assurance and testing protocols. This version has successfully integrated bitcoind's python functional tests into its multi-daemon process architecture. Interested developers can access the updated code and contribute to its ongoing development at [bitcoinbackbone.org](http://bitcoinbackbone.org).

Bitcoin Core has released version 30.3, which introduces various upgrades such as new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements. This version ensures greater compatibility with newer operating systems and has extensive support for multiple Linux, macOS, and Windows versions. Users and developers can download this latest version from [BitcoinCore.org](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.3/) and participate in its continuous improvement through the [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues) tracker.

Additionally, there is a focus on enhancing security measures for cryptocurrency transactions, particularly in the context of recovery mechanisms. The proposed strategies include using Xpub derivation-based recovery for BIP 32 based wallets and implementing stateful timestamped proofs to secure transactions against potential quantum computing threats. These innovative recovery schemes aim to provide comprehensive coverage for all network address types, maintaining the secrecy of the public keys and ensuring the integrity of transactions. Further details on these security enhancements are discussed in depth at [Delving Bitcoin](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/post-quantum-recovery-of-hashed-addresses-with-no-confiscatory-risk/2714/2).

recent_posts.title: new backbone code release with bitcoind python test framework integration
recent_posts.summary: - The 6th release of the backbone project enhances quality assurance and testing.  - Improved backbone-cli controls and optimizes internal command dispatch across daemons.  - Experiments with civkit cryptographic protocols aim to support a peer-to-peer bitcoin economy.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core 30.3 released
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin Core version 30.3 introduces new features, bug fixes, and performance enhancements.
- Upgrade guidance includes shutting down prior versions and follows system-specific installation steps.
- The update supports new Linux, macOS, and Windows versions and improves various software components.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core 29.4 released
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin Core version 29.4 is now available with numerous enhancements and bug fixes.
- Users should fully shut older versions before upgrading; support includes various operating systems.
- Significant changes include fixing a database issue and updates to transaction management and system documentation.

recent_posts.title: Post Quantum Recovery Of Hashed Addresses With No Confiscatory Risk
recent_posts.summary:
- The email outlines enhanced security for cryptocurrency with multiple recovery schemes.
- It introduces Xpub derivation-based recovery applicable to any BIP 32 based wallet.
- The sender seeks feedback on the proposal aiming for comprehensive recovery coverage.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Inquisition 29.4
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin Inquisition version 29.4 introduces support for key consensus changes, enhancing transaction security.
- These changes, implemented on default signet, have been activated progressively over three years.
- Users can connect with inquisition nodes to utilize these features by adjusting node configurations.

recent_posts.title: RFC: Block-Range Filters (a.k.a. Hierarchical filters)
recent_posts.summary:
- Advanced data structures improve querying sets, notably in approximate set membership queries.
- Paper highlights new sketching techniques for efficient multi-set querying with low false positives.
- Proposed structures facilitate rapid sync and efficient data sync in peer-to-peer networks.

active_posts.title: Quantum Recovery Of Hashed Address Secured Coins With No Confiscatory Risk
active_posts.summary:
- The discourse on quantum computing addresses cryptocurrency security through quantum-safe signatures.
- Proposals aim to protect ECC-based coins and ensure legitimate user access in a post-quantum scenario.
- No universal solution exists yet for recovery of coins secured by non-hashed addresses vulnerable to quantum attacks.

active_posts.title: BIP draft: CISA for Taproot Key Path Spends
active_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin Improvement Proposal introduces cross-input signature aggregation.  - This advancement keeps traditional script path spending and adds aggregation options.  - Developers and stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the proposal.

active_posts.title: Testnet 4 difficulty/hashrate
active_posts.summary:
- Testnet4's mining data shows large discrepancies in reported versus actual hashing difficulties.
- Nearly 90% of block confirmations are due to network propagation, not mining power.
- Optimal balance seen with one real block for every 10 to 12 min-difficulty blocks.

active_posts.title: Addressing the Diminishing Block Subsidy
active_posts.summary: - Bitcoin's security concerns rise as block subsidies diminish, proposing 0.25 BTC tail emission.  - The tail emission approach aims to balance miner income and reduce transaction fee volatility.  - Critics fear that exceeding the 21 million BTC cap could undermine Bitcoin's value store narrative.

active_posts.title: A Bitcoin-native LLM: dataset, architecture and open questions
active_posts.summary:
- The Bitcoin-native LLM aims to improve general-purpose models with specific protocol understanding.
- It requires a comprehensive dataset and bifurcated architecture for script analysis and live data queries.
- The project focuses on aiding developers and researchers, not on surveillance or transaction signing.

active_posts.title: [Research] A clockless vardiff strands a slowing miner
active_posts.summary:
- Variable difficulty in mining pools affects performance due to slow adjustment mechanisms.
- A new clock-based method proposed improves response by adjusting difficulty based on time.
- This hybrid approach enhances fairness and prevents miners from being stranded during low activity.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP174 extension proposal (Global Type: PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB_SIGNATURE)
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Jonathan Underwood proposed enhanced security measures in multisig discussions on GitHub.
- He debates that explicit signings in one-of-one multisig protect against potential exposures.
- Dmitry Petukhov contributes by recommending specific serial number indicators for single-sig.

today_in_history_posts.title: Trampoline Routing
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Trampoline routing in the lightning network involves using nodes to defer route calculation.
- This method allows fees and cltv requirements syncing through a gossip-based filter system.
- Despite higher fees, this approach enhances ease of use and payment reliability for users.

today_in_history_posts.title: Thoughts on scaling and consensus changes (2023)
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin is exploring off-chain "banks" to handle mass transactions and enhance scalability.
- These entities interconnect for liquidity but necessitate balance between cost and security.
- Diverse tools and networking ensure both compliance and operational safety in off-chain setups.
